text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Stocks had a mixed session in lackluster trade with activity capped ahead of next Tuesday's British budget and sentiment weighed by worries over interest rates and sterling. The FTSE 100 index closed 9.0 points lower at 3,953.8 with losers outweighing gainers by roughly five-to-four.

FRANKFURT - Stocks were pushed backwards and forwards as they tracked movements in the dollar, but dealers said volumes were limited and the market was probably entering a consolidation phase. The IBIS DAX slipped back to close at 2,764.85 points. Earlier, the DAX index ended market trade largely flat, paring earlier losses as the dollar pushed above 1.50 marks. It closed down 2.16 points at 2,772.34.

PARIS - Stocks closed just inside positive territory as profit-taking ahead of Friday's monthly settlement knocked them from their best levels. Wall Street's sell-off also hit sentiment. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 0.18 points, or 0.01 percent higher, at 2,233.57.

ZURICH - Stocks extended earlier losses after Wall Street slipped following the release of the Philadelphia Fed index. Dealers said stocks had already failed to move higher earlier despite gains on Wall Street Wednesday, adding that the market still appeared to be in a period of consolidation. The all-share SPI was down 12.26 points at 2,469.43.

TOKYO - Stocks ended a little lower as earlier gains racked up by strong demand for blue-chip issues evaporated due to profit-taking. The Ministry of Finance ordered Hanwa Bank to stop most operations, but the news had little impact on trade. The key Nikkei 225 finished at 21,143.34, down 46.62 points.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed weak after three consecutive record closes as the Hang Seng Index unsuccessfully tried to tackle resistance at 13,200 points. The index closed 67.60 points lower at 13,099.56 after a see-saw session which saw the index up at a record intraday high of 13,237.73 at one point then at a low of 13,028.03.

SYDNEY - Stocks deflated in the afternoon to close just lower as profit-takers pricked a record-breaking bubble formed in the morning session. Inspired by Wall Street's seemingly charmed run, enthusiastic buyers ensured the key indicator hurdled the 2,400-point barrier early. The All Ordinaries index closed 0.2 points lower at 2,392.5, barely changed from Wednesday's close.

JOHANNESBURG - A one-point hike in bank and prime lending rates took a heavy toll on stocks. Industrials were hit hardest, plunging 1.2 percent on the day after shedding 1 percent in the first 10 minutes of trade. The all-share index was dragged down with industrials. Golds followed the downhill slope, too, depressed by bullion. The industrial index plunged 97.2 points to 7,980.1, the all-shares fell 76.5 to 6,774.4 and golds shed 7.9 to 1,704.6.
